Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows a large, well-circumscribed mass that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, a classic radiographic sign indicating an extrapulmonary (e.g., pleural or chest wall) origin rather than an intrapulmonary one. This is confirmed by the CT scans (Figures 2 and 3) which demonstrate a discrete mass arising from the posterior thoracic cavity/pleura.
